title: Genesis Chapter 35 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 35 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 35 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 35.

questions.question: What command did God give to Jacob in Genesis 35:1?
options: Arise, go up to Bethel, and make an altar unto God
Go down to Egypt and dwell there
Build a city named after your brother Esau
Offer a sacrifice on Mount Sinai
questions.correctAnswer: Arise, go up to Bethel, and make an altar unto God
questions.explanation: God told Jacob to arise, go up to Bethel, and make an altar unto God, as stated in Genesis 35:1.

questions.question: What did Jacob instruct his household to do in Genesis 35:2?
options: Put away strange gods, be clean, and change garments
questions.correctAnswer: Put away strange gods, be clean, and change garments
questions.explanation: Jacob told his household to put away strange gods, be clean, and change their garments according to Genesis 35:2.

questions.question: In Genesis 35:3, what did Jacob promise to do when they arose and went up to Bethel?
options: Build a tower reaching to heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Make an altar unto God
questions.explanation: Jacob said he would make an altar unto God when they went up to Bethel, as recorded in Genesis 35:3.

questions.question: Where did Jacob hide the strange gods and earrings given to him by his household in Genesis 35:4?
options: Under the stone altar at Mamre
questions.correctAnswer: Under the oak by Shechem
questions.explanation: Jacob hid the strange gods and earrings under the oak which was by Shechem, as detailed in Genesis 35:4.

questions.question: What effect did the presence of Jacob and his people have on the surrounding cities according to Genesis 35:5?
options: The terror of God was upon the cities, so they did not pursue after Jacob's sons
The cities welcomed them with gifts
The cities formed an alliance with Jacob
questions.correctAnswer: The terror of God was upon the cities, so they did not pursue after Jacob's sons
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:5 states that the terror of God was upon the cities around and they did not pursue Jacob's sons.

questions.question: What new name did Jacob give to the place where he built an altar, as recorded in Genesis 35:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Elbethel
questions.explanation: Jacob called the place Elbethel because God appeared unto him there, according to Genesis 35:7.

questions.question: Who died and was buried beneath Bethel under an oak, named Allonbachuth in Genesis 35:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Deborah, Rebekah's nurse
questions.explanation: Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died and was buried beneath Bethel under an oak called Allonbachuth as noted in Genesis 35:8.

questions.question: True or False: God appeared to Jacob again after he came out of Padanaram and blessed him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:9 states God appeared to Jacob again after he came out of Padanaram and blessed him.

questions.question: What new name did God give Jacob in Genesis 35:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Israel
questions.explanation: God said Jacob's name shall be called Israel from then on, according to Genesis 35:10.

questions.question: According to Genesis 35:1, who had Jacob fled from when God appeared to him?
questions.correctAnswer: Esau, his brother
questions.explanation: God appeared to Jacob when he fled from the face of Esau his brother, as stated in Genesis 35:1.

questions.question: True or False: Jacob built an altar and called the place Bethel because God appeared to him there.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jacob called the place Elbethel after building the altar because God appeared to him there, not Bethel, as Genesis 35:7 explains.

questions.question: What did Jacob pour on the pillar he set up where God talked with him, according to Genesis 35:14?
questions.correctAnswer: A drink offering and oil
questions.explanation: Jacob poured a drink offering and oil on the stone pillar he set up where God talked with him, as described in Genesis 35:14.

questions.question: Who was born to Rachel in Genesis 35:17-18 despite her dying in childbirth?
questions.correctAnswer: Benjamin
questions.explanation: Rachel gave birth to Benjamin but died in childbirth, as narrated in Genesis 35:17-18.

questions.question: True or False: Jacob buried his father Isaac according to Genesis 35:29.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:29 states that Esau and Jacob buried Isaac after he died.

questions.question: In Genesis 35, which instruction comes before all others?
questions.correctAnswer: Go to Bethel
questions.explanation: God's first instruction to Jacob was to go up to Bethel, as seen in Genesis 35:1, before other commands like putting away strange gods or building an altar.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 35 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 35 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What promise does God make to Jacob concerning his descendants in Genesis 35?
options: He will be a great prophet
A nation and a company of nations shall be of him, and kings shall come out of his loins
He will never face hardship again
questions.correctAnswer: A nation and a company of nations shall be of him, and kings shall come out of his loins
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:11 clearly records God's promise to Jacob that he will be fruitful and multiply, producing a nation and company of nations, with kings coming from his lineage. This emphasizes God's covenant and blessing on Jacob's descendants.

questions.question: According to Genesis 35, what land does God promise to give Jacob and his descendants?
options: The land given to Abraham and Isaac
The land near the Red Sea
questions.correctAnswer: The land given to Abraham and Isaac
questions.explanation: God promises Jacob the land which He gave to Abraham and Isaac, and to his seed after him, as stated in Genesis 35:12. This shows the continuity of God's covenant through generations.

questions.question: What did Jacob do at the place where God talked with him after the blessing in Genesis 35?
options: Set up a pillar of stone and poured a drink offering and oil on it
questions.correctAnswer: Set up a pillar of stone and poured a drink offering and oil on it
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:14 describes Jacob setting up a stone pillar at the place where God spoke to him, and pouring a drink offering and oil on it, signifying an act of worship and remembrance of God's presence.

questions.question: Why did Jacob name the place Bethel according to Genesis 35?
options: Because he built a house there
Because God appeared unto him there when he fled from his brother
Because it was a place of victory
Because it was the land of his ancestors
questions.correctAnswer: Because God appeared unto him there when he fled from his brother
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:15 explains that Jacob called the place Bethel because God appeared to him there when he fled from Esau, highlighting the significance of God's presence and protection.

questions.question: What event happened to Rachel as they journeyed from Bethel in Genesis 35?
options: She had hard labour and died
She gave birth to twins safely
questions.correctAnswer: She had hard labour and died
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:16-19 narrate that Rachel travailed with hard labour, and as she died, she named her son Benoni, but Jacob called him Benjamin. She was buried near Ephrath, showing the cost and sorrow in their journey.

questions.question: How does the passage from Genesis 35:16-19 teach about trust in God during times of suffering?
options: It shows that faith includes enduring hardship with God's presence
It suggests that suffering means God has abandoned you
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that faith includes enduring hardship with God's presence
questions.explanation: The story of Rachel's hard labour and death in Genesis 35:16-19 illustrates that even amid suffering, God’s purposes continue, and trust involves enduring difficult times, as Jacob still names the child and sets a pillar to honor her memory.

questions.question: What did Jacob do to honor Rachel after her death according to Genesis 35?
options: Set a pillar upon her grave
questions.correctAnswer: Set a pillar upon her grave
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:20 states that Jacob set up a pillar on Rachel's grave to honor her memory, showing respect and remembrance for her life and death.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 35, Jacob called his son Benjamin because Rachel named him so before she died.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:18 explains that Rachel called her son Benoni as her soul was departing, but Jacob called him Benjamin instead.

questions.question: What is the significance of the drink offering and oil poured on the pillar Jacob set up in Genesis 35?
options: It was a form of idolatry
It signified consecration and worship to God
It was a common agricultural practice
It was a way to mark territory
questions.correctAnswer: It signified consecration and worship to God
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:14 describes Jacob pouring a drink offering and oil on the stone pillar, which was a ritual act symbolizing consecration and worship to God, reflecting reverence and commitment.

questions.question: What does Genesis 35:13 teach about God's interaction with Jacob at Bethel?
options: God departed from Jacob after blessing him
God told Jacob to build a city
God gave Jacob a new wife
questions.correctAnswer: God departed from Jacob after blessing him
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:13 states that God went up from Jacob in the place where He talked with him, indicating that after blessing Jacob, God departed, marking the completion of the encounter.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 35 describes a time when Jacob obeyed God's command to purify his household before building an altar.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Though this event is described earlier in Genesis 35:2-4, the chapter overall shows Jacob’s obedience in purifying his household by removing strange gods before building the altar, demonstrating faith and integrity.

questions.question: According to Genesis 35, what does the renaming of Jacob to Israel signify about his relationship with God?
options: A new identity as a deceiver
A transformation to one who struggles with God and prevails
That he would live in isolation
That he would only have one son
questions.correctAnswer: A transformation to one who struggles with God and prevails
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:10 recounts God renaming Jacob as Israel, meaning 'he who struggles with God,' marking a new covenant identity reflecting his spiritual transformation and favor with God.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the teaching about humility found in the events surrounding Rachel’s death in Genesis 35?
options: Humility involves trusting God’s plan even in loss and sorrow
Humility is only about public acts of worship
questions.correctAnswer: Humility involves trusting God’s plan even in loss and sorrow
questions.explanation: Rachel’s death during childbirth (Genesis 35:16-19) and Jacob’s response by naming the child Benjamin and setting a pillar show humility through trust in God’s sovereign plan despite personal tragedy.

questions.question: What lesson about obedience and blessing can be drawn from Genesis 35:11-12 about God's promises?
options: Obedience to God’s call leads to fruitful blessings and inheritance
Obedience is optional for God’s promises
Obedience only benefits the individual, not descendants
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God’s call leads to fruitful blessings and inheritance
questions.explanation: When Jacob obeys God, Genesis 35:11-12 records God’s promise of fruitfulness, nations, kings, and land inheritance, illustrating that obedience is key to receiving God’s covenantal blessings.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 35 teaches that declaring God’s promises publicly, like Jacob setting up a pillar, helps strengthen faith and witness.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jacob’s act of setting up a stone pillar and naming the place Bethel (Genesis 35:14-15) serves as a public declaration of God’s presence and promises, encouraging faith and testimony.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 35 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 35.

questions.question: Which location did Israel spread his tent beyond, according to Genesis 35?
questions.correctAnswer: The tower of Edar
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:21 states that Israel journeyed and spread his tent beyond the tower of Edar, marking the place where he dwelt.

questions.question: What grave sin did Reuben commit while Israel dwelt in that land?
options: He lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine
questions.correctAnswer: He lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:22 reveals that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine, a serious breach of family and cultural honor.

questions.question: How many sons did Jacob have according to Genesis 35?
questions.correctAnswer: Twelve
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:22 clearly states that the sons of Jacob were twelve in number.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as one of Leah's sons in Genesis 35?
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:23 lists Leah's sons as Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun. Joseph is not among them; he is Rachel's son (Genesis 35:24).

questions.question: Who were the sons of Rachel mentioned in Genesis 35?
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph and Benjamin
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:24 identifies Joseph and Benjamin as the sons of Rachel.

questions.question: Which handmaid’s sons were Dan and Naphtali?
questions.correctAnswer: Rachel's handmaid Bilhah
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:25 states that Dan and Naphtali were the sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid.

questions.question: From which region were all the sons of Jacob born?
questions.correctAnswer: Padanaram
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:26 explains that the sons of Jacob were born in Padanaram, highlighting the family's sojourn there before returning to Canaan.

questions.question: To whom did Jacob come when he returned to the land of Canaan?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaac, his father
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:27 states that Jacob came to Isaac his father at Mamre, in the city of Arbah (Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had sojourned.

questions.question: How long did Isaac live according to Genesis 35?
questions.correctAnswer: 180 years
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:28 records that Isaac’s days were an hundred and fourscore (180) years.

questions.question: Who buried Isaac after he died?
options: Only his sons Simeon and Levi
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob and Esau together
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:29 tells us that Isaac was buried by his sons Esau and Jacob together, signifying reconciliation between the brothers after many years.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God changing Jacob’s name to Israel and establishes the covenant promise?
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 32:28
questions.explanation: Genesis 32:28 records the initial renaming of Jacob to Israel by the angel, which is reaffirmed in Genesis 35:10, emphasizing God’s covenant with him.

questions.question: In Genesis 35, what is the significance of the pillar Jacob set up at Bethel, and which literary device does this represent?
questions.correctAnswer: A covenant altar representing inclusio
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:14-15 describes Jacob setting up a stone pillar and naming the place Bethel, which serves as an inclusio framing his encounters with God at Bethel (also in Genesis 28), marking covenantal moments.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the name 'Bethel,' the place where God appeared to Jacob?
questions.correctAnswer: House of God
questions.explanation: 'Bethel' literally means 'House of God' in Hebrew, as reflected in Genesis 35:1 and 35:15 where Jacob builds an altar and names the place because God appeared to him there.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 35, Rachel died while giving birth to Benjamin and was buried near Bethlehem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:18-19 records that Rachel died in childbirth and was buried on the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.

questions.question: True or False: The sons of Jacob were all born in the land of Canaan.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:26 states that the sons of Jacob were born in Padanaram, not in Canaan, highlighting their birth during Jacob’s sojourn in Aram.

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 35 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 35 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is emphasized by Jacob instructing his household to put away strange gods and change their garments before going to Bethel?
options: The necessity of external rituals for salvation
The importance of physical cleanliness over spiritual
The rejection of God's covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification and separation from idolatry
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:2 shows Jacob commanding his household to remove strange gods and cleanse themselves, highlighting the doctrine of sanctification—being set apart from sin and idolatry as a preparation to worship God (cf. 2 Corinthians 6:17).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by the 'terror of God' upon the cities around Jacob's journey?
options: God's holiness and power to protect His people
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and power to protect His people
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:5 states the terror of God was upon surrounding cities so they did not pursue Jacob's sons, illustrating God's holiness that commands reverence and His power to protect His covenant people (cf. Exodus 14:14).

questions.question: How does God’s renaming of Jacob to Israel in Genesis 35:10 relate to the doctrine of divine election?
options: It signifies God's sovereign choice and new identity for His chosen servant
It indicates a complete change of personality and nature
It represents a human decision to change one's destiny
It nullifies all previous covenants made with Jacob
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies God's sovereign choice and new identity for His chosen servant
questions.explanation: In Genesis 35:10, God changes Jacob's name to Israel, symbolizing divine election and covenantal identity, affirming God's sovereign choice in salvation history (cf. Romans 9:11-13).

questions.question: What theological significance does God’s self-revelation as 'God Almighty' in Genesis 35:11 carry?
options: It reveals God's omnipotence and covenant faithfulness
It limits God’s power to only the land of Canaan
It denies God's ability to bless nations
It shows that God is distant and uninvolved
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals God's omnipotence and covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:11 reveals God as El Shaddai (God Almighty), emphasizing His unlimited power and commitment to bless and multiply Jacob's descendants, demonstrating covenant faithfulness (cf. Genesis 17:1).

questions.question: What connection does the burial of Rachel in Genesis 35:19 have to the larger redemptive narrative of Scripture?
options: It foreshadows the sorrow and loss that accompany God’s promises
It marks the end of God's covenant with Abraham
It indicates the failure of God's promises to Jacob
It signifies the abolition of mourning in God's kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the sorrow and loss that accompany God’s promises
questions.explanation: Rachel's death and burial in Genesis 35:19 underscore that even amidst God’s covenant promises, human suffering and loss occur, prefiguring the suffering inherent in the redemptive story culminating in Christ (cf. John 16:33).

questions.question: What doctrinal insight arises from the combined promises in Genesis 35:11 and 35:12 regarding Jacob’s descendants and the land?
options: God’s covenant is both personal and territorial, promising nationhood and land
God’s promises depend on human merit and works
The land promise is temporary and conditional on Israel’s obedience alone
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant is both personal and territorial, promising nationhood and land
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:11-12 together reveal God's covenantal promise of fruitful descendants (nation and company of nations) and the inheritance of land, highlighting God’s faithfulness to both people and place (cf. Deuteronomy 7:13).

questions.question: How does Jacob’s act of setting up a stone pillar and pouring a drink offering and oil in Genesis 35:14 reflect Old Testament worship theology?
options: It symbolizes a memorial and consecration of a holy place
It indicates a magical ritual to gain favor
It denies the necessity of spiritual worship
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes a memorial and consecration of a holy place
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:14 shows Jacob setting up a pillar and offering drink and oil as a memorial and dedication of Bethel, reflecting Old Testament worship theology where physical symbols mark divine encounters (cf. Joshua 4:20-24).

questions.question: What does the naming of the place 'Elbethel' by Jacob in Genesis 35:7 reveal about his understanding of God’s revelation?
options: Jacob acknowledges God’s appearance and presence at that location
Jacob denies God’s presence in that place
Jacob names it after a pagan god
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob acknowledges God’s appearance and presence at that location
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:7 shows Jacob naming the altar Elbethel, meaning 'God of Bethel,' which indicates his recognition and remembrance of God’s manifest presence and revelation there (cf. Exodus 3:5).

questions.question: What does the incident of Reuben lying with Bilhah in Genesis 35:22 teach about human sin and its impact within God’s covenant family?
options: Sin can occur even in God’s chosen family, showing human fallibility
Sin is impossible among God’s elect
questions.correctAnswer: Sin can occur even in God’s chosen family, showing human fallibility
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:22 records Reuben’s sin with Bilhah, indicating that human sinfulness affects even the covenant family, underscoring the need for grace and redemption (cf. Romans 3:23).

questions.question: How do Genesis 35:9 and 35:13 together demonstrate God’s covenantal faithfulness to Jacob?
options: God appears again to bless Jacob and then departs, affirming His promises
God abandons Jacob immediately after blessing him
God changes His promises to Jacob
God’s presence is temporary and unreliable
questions.correctAnswer: God appears again to bless Jacob and then departs, affirming His promises
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:9 and 35:13 show God appearing again to Jacob to bless him and then departing, illustrating the certainty and personal nature of God’s covenantal faithfulness (cf. Hebrews 6:13-18).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the story of Jacob’s blessings and name change is merely mythological with no theological significance. What does Genesis 35:10-11 actually teach about God’s purpose for Jacob?
options: It teaches that God sovereignly redefines Jacob’s identity and mission to be a father of nations
It shows that Jacob’s name change was a human invention with no divine input
It indicates that God’s promises are vague and unclear
It suggests that the story has no connection to Israel’s origins
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that God sovereignly redefines Jacob’s identity and mission to be a father of nations
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:10-11 records God renaming Jacob as Israel and promising him nationhood and kingship, affirming a divinely ordained identity and mission, countering sceptical claims of myth (cf. Romans 9:6-13).

questions.question: What theological significance does the burial of Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, under the oak called Allonbachuth in Genesis 35:8 have in biblical symbolism?
options: It symbolizes mourning and the fragility of human life amidst God's covenant
It indicates that trees were objects of worship
It celebrates the triumph of pagan religion
It denies God’s care for individuals
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes mourning and the fragility of human life amidst God's covenant
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:8 mentions Deborah's burial under an oak named Allonbachuth ('oak of weeping'), symbolizing mourning and the reality of death even within God’s covenant community (cf. John 11:35).

questions.question: How does Genesis 35:4, where Jacob hides the strange gods and earrings under the oak by Shechem, contribute to the understanding of idolatry and purification in the Old Testament?
options: It demonstrates the need to remove and hide idols to restore covenant purity
It shows that idols are acceptable if hidden
It implies that personal possessions are more important than God
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates the need to remove and hide idols to restore covenant purity
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:4 shows Jacob hiding strange gods and earrings, symbolizing the removal of idolatry to maintain covenant purity and obedience to God’s commands (cf. Exodus 20:3-5).

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching about death and hope can be drawn from Rachel naming her son Benoni but Jacob calling him Benjamin in Genesis 35:18?
options: It reflects the tension between human sorrow and divine hope in salvation
It indicates that human naming has no significance
It shows that death ends all hope
It teaches that parents have no role in naming children
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the tension between human sorrow and divine hope in salvation
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:18 records Rachel naming her son Benoni ('son of my sorrow') as she dies, but Jacob naming him Benjamin ('son of the right hand'), symbolizing the tension between human grief and God’s hopeful promise of salvation (cf. Psalms 30:5).

questions.question: What narrative-theological significance does Jacob’s journey to his father Isaac in Genesis 35:27-29 have within the broader redemptive story?
options: It connects the patriarchal promises and continuity of God’s covenant across generations
It ends the covenantal promises made to Abraham
It shows the failure of God’s promises
It disconnects Jacob from his heritage
questions.correctAnswer: It connects the patriarchal promises and continuity of God’s covenant across generations
questions.explanation: Genesis 35:27-29 shows Jacob returning to Isaac and burying him, symbolizing the continuity of the Abrahamic covenant and God’s redemptive plan through generations (cf. Hebrews 11:9-12).
